ei.title: Chapter 5-14 Analysis: Why Bystanders Don't Intervene
ei.subject: 올림포스독해의기본1

fullPassage: Social psychology tells us that bystanders in emergency situations are acting normally when they fail to respond. We would fail to respond as well. That social psychological insight makes us uncomfortable. We like to feel we would behave differently, better. The problem with bystanders, however, does not stem from defects in their character that prevent them from helping. Rather, the situation that bystanders find themselves in constrains their behavior more than we realize. For example, the more bystanders there are, the less likely any one of them will intervene. A single bystander at the scene of an emergency would usually respond, just as we hope we would. But when a number of bystanders witness an emergency, responsibility apparently diffuses among them, getting weaker. No one bystander feels enough personal responsibility to respond.

questions.passage: Social psychology ①<u>tells</u> us that bystanders in emergency situations are acting normally when they fail to respond. We would fail to respond as well. That social psychological insight makes us uncomfortable. We like to feel we would behave differently, better. The problem with bystanders, however, does not stem from defects in their character that prevent them from helping. Rather, the situation that bystanders find themselves in ②<u>constrains</u> their behavior more than we realize. For example, the ③<u>most bystanders</u> there are, the less likely any one of them will ④<u>intervene</u>. A single bystander at the scene of an emergency would usually respond, just as we hope we would. But when a number of bystanders witness an emergency, responsibility apparently diffuses among them, getting weaker. No one bystander feels enough personal responsibility to respond.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: most bystanders → more bystanders
det.analysis:
① tells — 단수주어 Social psychology + tells 정상
② constrains — 단수주어 the situation + constrains 정상
③ most bystanders — 원문 more bystanders, 'the 비교급 ~, the 비교급 …' 구문이라 비교급 more ←정답
④ intervene — 조동사 will 뒤 동사원형 정상
det.tip: the + 비교급 ~, the + 비교급 … = ~할수록 더 …하다. 여기서는 최상급 most가 아니라 비교급 more가 맞아요.

questions.passage: Social psychology tells us that bystanders in emergency situations are acting normally when they fail to respond. We would fail to respond as well. That social psychological insight makes us uncomfortable. We like to feel we would behave ①<u>differently</u>, better. The problem with bystanders, however, does not stem from defects in their character that prevent them from helping. Rather, the situation that bystanders find ②<u>themselves</u> in constrains their behavior more than we realize. For example, the more bystanders there are, the less likely any one of them will intervene. A single bystander at the scene of an emergency would usually respond, just as we hope we would. But when a number of bystanders ③<u>witness</u> an emergency, responsibility apparently diffuses among them, ④<u>get weaker</u>. No one bystander feels enough personal responsibility to respond.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: get weaker → getting weaker
det.analysis:
① differently — 동사 behave를 꾸미는 부사 정상
② themselves — 주어와 목적어가 같아 재귀대명사 정상
③ witness — 주어 bystanders(복수) + witness 정상
④ get weaker — 원문 getting weaker, 콤마 뒤에서 '점점 약해지면서'를 뜻하는 분사구문이라 현재분사 getting ←정답
det.tip: 콤마 뒤 '~하면서'는 분사구문(-ing). '...diffuses ..., getting weaker'는 '흩어지면서 점점 약해진다'는 뜻이에요. get(원형)이 오면 동사가 두 개라 문장이 깨져요.

questions.passage: Social psychology tells us that bystanders in emergency situations are acting normally when they fail to respond. We would fail to respond as well. That social psychological insight makes us uncomfortable. We like to feel we would behave differently, better. The problem with bystanders, however, does not stem from defects in their character that prevent them from helping. Rather, the ①<u>situation what</u> bystanders ②<u>find</u> themselves in constrains their behavior more than we realize. For example, the more bystanders there are, the less likely any one of them ③<u>will</u> intervene. A single bystander at the scene of an emergency would usually respond, just as we hope we would. But when a number of bystanders witness an emergency, responsibility apparently diffuses among them, getting weaker. No one bystander ④<u>feels</u> enough personal responsibility to respond.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: situation what → situation that
det.analysis:
① situation what — 원문 situation that, 선행사 the situation가 있으므로 목적격 관계대명사 that(전치사 in의 목적어)이 맞다. what은 선행사를 이미 품은 관계대명사라 the situation 뒤에 올 수 없음 ←정답
② find — 주어 bystanders(복수) + find 정상
③ will — 조동사 will + intervene 정상
④ feels — 주어 No one bystander(단수) + feels 정상
det.tip: what은 '~하는 것'이라 그 자체에 선행사가 들어 있어요(the thing which). 앞에 the situation처럼 선행사가 이미 있으면 that/which를 써요.

questions.passage: Social psychology tells us that bystanders in ①<u>emergency</u> situations are ②<u>acting strangely</u> when they fail to respond. We would fail to respond as well. That social psychological insight makes us uncomfortable. We like to feel we would behave differently, better. The problem with bystanders, however, does not stem from defects in their character that ③<u>prevent</u> them from helping. Rather, the situation that bystanders find themselves in constrains their behavior more than we realize. For example, the more bystanders there are, the less likely any one of them will intervene. A single bystander at the scene of an emergency would usually respond, just as we hope we would. But when a number of bystanders ④<u>witness</u> an emergency, responsibility apparently diffuses among them, getting weaker. No one bystander feels enough personal responsibility to respond.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: 본문의 핵심은 방관자가 반응하지 않을 때 '정상적으로(normally)' 행동한다는 것이므로 'strangely(이상하게)'는 반대이다.
det.analysis:
① emergency — 응급 상황, 원문 일치
② acting strangely — 원문은 acting normally(정상적으로 행동), 무반응이 오히려 정상이라는 게 요지 ←정답
③ prevent — 막다, 원문 일치
④ witness — 목격하다, 원문 일치
det.tip: acting normally = (무반응이라도) 정상적으로 행동함 ↔ strangely(이상하게)

questions.passage: Social psychology tells us that bystanders in emergency situations are acting normally when they fail to respond. We would fail to respond as well. That social psychological ①<u>insight</u> makes us uncomfortable. We like to feel we would behave differently, better. The problem with bystanders, however, does not stem from defects in their character that ②<u>prevent</u> them from helping. Rather, the situation that bystanders find themselves in ③<u>liberates</u> their behavior more than we realize. For example, the more bystanders there are, the less likely any one of them will intervene. A single bystander at the scene of an emergency would usually respond, just as we hope we would. But when a number of bystanders witness an emergency, responsibility apparently ④<u>diffuses</u> among them, getting weaker. No one bystander feels enough personal responsibility to respond.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: 상황이 방관자의 행동을 '제약한다(constrains)'는 것이 요지이므로 'liberates(자유롭게 하다)'는 반대이다.
det.analysis:
① insight — 통찰, 원문 일치
② prevent — 막다, 원문 일치
③ liberates — 원문은 constrains(제약하다), 상황이 행동을 옭아맨다는 맥락 ←정답
④ diffuses — 흩어지다, 원문 일치
det.tip: constrains(제약하다) ↔ liberates(해방하다). 상황이 행동을 '풀어준다'면 방관자 효과 설명과 어긋나요.

questions.passage: Social psychology tells us that bystanders in emergency situations are acting normally when they fail to respond. We would fail to respond as well. That social psychological insight __________. We like to feel we would behave differently, better. The problem with bystanders, however, does not stem from defects in their character that prevent them from helping. Rather, the situation that bystanders find themselves in constrains their behavior more than we realize. For example, the more bystanders there are, the less likely any one of them will intervene. A single bystander at the scene of an emergency would usually respond, just as we hope we would. But when a number of bystanders witness an emergency, responsibility apparently diffuses among them, getting weaker. No one bystander feels enough personal responsibility to respond.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 우리도 방관자처럼 반응하지 못할 것이라는 통찰은 우리를 '불편하게 만든다'.
det.analysis:
❌ ① proves that we are usually right — 우리가 옳음을 증명한다 (우리도 실패한다는 내용과 반대)
❌ ② has little real evidence behind it — 근거가 거의 없다 (본문은 사회심리학적 통찰로 제시, 반대)
❌ ③ excites us about helping others — 돕는 것에 들뜨게 한다 (감정 방향이 반대)
✅ ④ makes us uncomfortable — 우리를 불편하게 만든다 ←정답
det.tip: 우리도 똑같이 무반응할 거라는 '불편한 진실' → makes us uncomfortable

ch: proves that we are usually right
has little real evidence behind it

questions.passage: Social psychology tells us that bystanders in emergency situations are acting normally when they fail to respond. We would fail to respond as well. A single bystander __________ would usually respond, just as we hope we would. But when a number of bystanders witness an emergency, responsibility apparently diffuses among them, getting weaker. questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 혼자인 방관자는 '응급 상황 현장에서' 우리가 바라는 대로 대개 반응한다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① at the scene of an emergency — 응급 상황 현장에서 ←정답
❌ ② far away from any real danger — 위험에서 멀리 (현장에 있어야 반응, 반대)
❌ ③ long after the crowd has gone — 무리가 떠난 뒤 (본문에 없는 상황)
❌ ④ without any sense of duty — 아무 의무감 없이 (혼자면 오히려 책임을 느껴 반응, 반대)
det.tip: A single bystander at the scene ~ would usually respond = 혼자 현장에 있으면 대개 반응함

ch: at the scene of an emergency
far away from any real danger
long after the crowd has gone

questions.stem: 다음 글의 내용과 일치하는 것은?

det.korean: 본문은 '우리도 마찬가지로 반응하지 못할 것(We would fail to respond as well)'이라고 인정한다.
det.analysis:
① 본문은 무반응을 normally(정상)로 봄 → 비정상 규정은 왜곡
② We would fail to respond as well — 원문 일치 ←정답
③ 혼자인 방관자는 대개 반응함(반대)
④ 방관자가 많을수록 책임은 분산되어 약해짐(반대)
det.tip: 핵심: '우리라고 다르지 않다' — 상황이 같으면 우리도 무반응

ch: 사회심리학은 방관자의 무반응을 비정상적 행동으로 규정한다.
우리도 같은 상황에 놓이면 반응하지 못할 것이다.
방관자가 혼자일 때는 오히려 잘 반응하지 않는다.
책임감은 방관자의 수가 많을수록 더 강해진다.

questions.stem: 다음 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?

det.korean: 본문은 책임이 분산되어 '약해진다(getting weaker)'고 하므로, 각자가 더 큰 책임을 느낀다는 것은 불일치이다.
det.analysis:
① responsibility apparently diffuses ... getting weaker — 일치
② the situation ... constrains their behavior more than we realize — 일치
③ 방관자가 많을수록 개인 책임은 오히려 약해짐 → 더 큰 책임을 느낀다는 것은 반대 ←정답(불일치)
④ We like to feel we would behave differently, better — 일치
det.tip: diffuse + getting weaker = 분산되어 약해짐 (개인 책임 ↓)

ch: 책임이 여러 명 사이로 분산되면 점점 약해진다.
방관자의 행동은 성격보다 상황의 영향을 더 받는다.
방관자가 많을수록 각자가 더 큰 책임을 느낀다.
우리는 남들과 다르게, 더 낫게 행동하고 싶어 한다.

questions.stem: 다음 글의 내용과 일치하는 것은?

det.korean: 방관자가 많을수록 책임이 분산되어 개입할 가능성이 낮아진다.
det.analysis:
① 문제는 성격 결함에서 비롯되지 않음(반대)
② 여럿이면 오히려 아무도 안 나섬(반대)
③ 통찰은 우리를 uncomfortable(불편)하게 함(반대)
④ the more bystanders ~ the less likely ~ intervene / responsibility diffuses — 원문 일치 ←정답
det.tip: 방관자 ↑ → 책임 분산 → 개입 ↓ (방관자 효과)

ch: 방관자 효과는 개인의 도덕적 결함으로 설명된다.
응급 상황에서는 방관자 수와 상관없이 누군가 반드시 돕는다.
방관자가 많아지면 책임이 분산되어 개입 가능성이 낮아진다.

questions.stem: 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 본문은 방관자가 나서지 않는 이유가 성격 결함이 아니라, 여럿이 있을 때 책임이 분산되는 상황 때문이라고 설명한다.
det.analysis:
① 성격이 아니라 상황(책임 분산)이 원인 — 글 전체 핵심 ←정답
② 대처 요령을 알려주는 글이 아님
③ 실험 방법론을 다루지 않음
④ 이타성의 진화적 기원은 언급 없음
det.tip: 원인 = 성격(character)이 아니라 상황(책임의 분산)

ch: 방관자의 무반응은 성격이 아니라 책임 분산이라는 상황에서 비롯된다는 점

questions.stem: 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 본문은 목격자(방관자)가 많을수록 책임이 분산되어 도움이 줄어든다는 방관자 효과를 설명한다.
det.analysis:

det.tip: 제목 = 방관자(목격자)가 많을수록 도움 ↓ → Why More Witnesses Mean Less Help

questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 diffuses among them이 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: diffuse는 기체가 퍼지듯 '흩어져 옅어지다'라는 뜻으로, 책임이 여럿에게 나뉘어 각자가 느끼는 몫이 약해짐을 비유한다.
det.analysis:
❌ ① 책임이 더 커진다 — getting weaker(약해짐)와 반대
❌ ② 한 사람에게 집중된다 — 분산(diffuse)의 반대

questions.passage: Social psychology tells us that bystanders in emergency situations are acting normally when they fail to respond. We would fail to respond as well. That social psychological insight makes us uncomfortable. We like to feel we would behave differently, better. The problem with bystanders, however, does not stem from defects in their character that prevent them from helping. Rather, the situation that bystanders find themselves in constrains their behavior more than we realize. For example, the more bystanders there are, the less likely <u>any one of them</u> will intervene. A single bystander at the scene of an emergency would usually respond, just as we hope we would. But when a number of bystanders witness an emergency, responsibility apparently diffuses among them, getting weaker. No one bystander feels enough personal responsibility to respond.
